CyberPi uploader

Write Python for your Makeblock CyberPi and mBot2 in VS Code, then send it to the robot with one keystroke. No mBlock, no mLink, nothing else to install.

three steps to the robot.

  1. 01

    Plug in

    Connect the CyberPi with a USB data cable and switch it on. Quit mBlock if it's open: it holds the port.
  2. 02

    Press ⌘⌥U

    Open a .py file and press ⌘⌥U, or click the upload icon. Pick the port the first time; we remember it.
  3. 03

    Watch it run

    The CyberPi restarts with your program. Anything it prints appears in the CyberPi panel in VS Code.

made to stay out of the way.

  • Upload from where you write

    The editor title bar, the status bar, the Explorer's right-click menu or the Command Palette. Whichever is closest.

  • Nothing else to install

    The serial driver is built in for Apple silicon and Intel Macs. No Python, mLink or mBlock needed.

  • See what it prints

    A serial monitor shows your program's print() output as the robot runs it.

  • Safe uploads

    Programs land in a staging slot first, so a failed upload leaves your last program in place.

your first program.

Start every program from an @event handler, the way mBlock does. The extension warns you before uploading a file without one.

Press ⌘⌥U. The screen says Hello, the LEDs turn green and ready appears in the output panel.

Want autocomplete for cyberpi, mbot2 and mbuild? Add type stubs to your project and VS Code's Python extension does the rest.

Read the guide

how it works.

The extension speaks the same USB serial protocol as mBlock 5, straight from VS Code.

  1. 01

    Upload mode

    It switches the CyberPi into upload mode and prepares it, as mBlock does.

  2. 02

    Send

    Your file goes to a staging slot in 80-byte blocks. Each block is checked and acknowledged before the next.

  3. 03

    Restart

    The board restarts and swaps in the new program. If anything fails on the way, the old one stays.

Frame formats, checksums and tests are in the protocol notes. Thanks to dachrisch/mbot2-course-setup for first decoding mBlock's upload sequence.

if something's not right.

It can't find the CyberPi.
Run ls /dev/cu.* in Terminal with the CyberPi switched on. If nothing like cu.usbserial-… appears, try another cable. Many USB-C cables only charge.
It says the port is busy.
Quit mBlock 5 and mLink, or stop the serial monitor with “CyberPi: Start / Stop Serial Monitor”.
The old program still runs.
Switch the CyberPi off and on. The new program starts from the staging slot on the next boot.
Does it work on Windows or Linux?
Not yet. It's built and tested for macOS.

Still stuck? Open an issue and include what the CyberPi panel shows.
